To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the STS/ STSE approach associated with teaching Chemistry, in the perspective of significant learning, has been little used, although it has been proven to be a promising approach, which promotes critical reflection and the development of scientific literacy in the context of the teaching-learning process.

STS and STSE approaches in the teaching of chemistry, in the perspective of significant learning, are still incipient in the national scenario and that there is a need for more studies in the area to promote a better understanding of the theme and the development of teaching practices that involve the theme of pesticides in the classroom.

the STS/ STSE perspective and meaningful learning have been used in Chemistry education to promote the development of critical thinking and reflection of students about the influences of science and technology on society.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the need to promote changes in the teaching of science in the perspective of STS/STES, with a focus on the theme of agrotoxics and meaningful learning, as a strategy to promote the development of critical awareness of students regarding science and technology in the context of society.

the need to promote the development of critical awareness of the student regarding the social, economic and cultural aspects involved in the teaching of chemistry, in order to develop in him the capacity for reflection and the construction of his own knowledge, through meaningful learning.

the need to rethink the teaching of Chemistry, considering the STS/ STSE approach, as a strategy for the development of meaningful learning in the classroom, in order to promote critical and reflective awareness in students about the influences of science and technology on society, in the perspective of the development of a citizenship capable of acting in the context of a democratic society.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the STS/ STSE approach associated with meaningful learning is an important strategy to promote the contextualization of the teaching of chemistry, in addition to being a tool to stimulate the development of critical, analytical and reflexive thinking of the students.

the application of the STS/ STSE approach in the teaching of chemistry in the perspective of significant learning has been incorporated into teaching and has been a great challenge to teachers, who have been working in the field of education.

, despite the advances in the application of the STS/STS perspective in the teaching of chemistry, it is still necessary to deepen the studies on the subject, in view of the importance of the theme of agrotoxics for the society.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the STS/ STSE approach in teaching Chemistry in the perspective and meaningful learning has the potential to promote the development of critical awareness and the construction of knowledge in students, however, there is still a lot to be done in the field of education, especially in the area of science education, to overcome the difficulties of the teacher in the process of teaching-learning and the lack of preparation of students in the area of Natural Sciences, in order to improve the quality of teaching.

the STS approach in the teaching of chemistry has the potential to contribute to the development of critical awareness of students regarding influences on science and technologies in society, although this approach is still in its initial stage of development and implementation.

the STS/STS approach associated with the teaching of chemistry in the perspective of significant learning has the potential to develop students' critical thinking, which is fundamental to the development of a democratic and participative society.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the STS/STSSE approach, associated with the pesticide topic, in the perspective of the significant learning of Chemistry, can contribute significantly to students' understanding of the theme, and also to the development of their critical thinking.

the application of the STS/SE approach in the teaching of chemistry, articulated to the theme of pesticides, can contribute to the development of students’ critical and reflective awareness about the influences of science and technology in the society, in addition to the development of significant learning.

the STSE approach, articulated with meaningful learning, can be used to teach Chemistry, in order to promote the development of critical awareness of students, as well as the construction of knowledge that is more relevant to their lives.
